company_items.summary: AutoZone beat FQ4 EPS estimates ($56.05 vs. $54.03 expected), but the beat was low quality — driven by a 145 basis point tariff refund tailwind and a 105 basis point non-cash LIFO benefit to gross margins. Domestic comps missed badly at +1.6% vs. +3.1% expected, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management noted improving sales linearity in the back half of the quarter and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027.

Cognex announced it will acquire RealSense, described as the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional $106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80–90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal expands Cognex's footprint into high-growth Physical AI and robotics perception markets.

MillerKnoll beat FQ1 EPS estimates solidly (53 cents vs. 36 cents expected), and crucially would have beaten even without tariff refund help — excluding the 11-cent tailwind, EPS was 42 cents vs. 36 cents expected. Sales missed, declining 3.3% organically to $923.4 million vs. $943.2 million expected, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Fiscal 2027 revenue guidance was trimmed slightly while the EPS band was held unchanged, and FQ2 EPS guidance midpoint of 46 cents is in line with consensus.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO, effective November 1, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman staying through the transition. Hau brings prior CFO experience at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. The announcement is a routine leadership transition with no financial guidance update.

THOR Industries missed FQ4 EPS estimates (78 cents vs. 87 cents expected) as gross margins fell 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4%, well below the 13.85% expected, even as revenue came in slightly above the Street at $2.311 billion. Management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflation pressuring household budgets, and declined to offer formal fiscal 2027 guidance. Bright spots included healthy dealer inventory levels, ongoing structural cost actions, and a roughly 75% year-over-year surge in the North American towable RV order backlog.

Viking Therapeutics shares spiked in pre-market trading after reporting positive clinical trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in trial participants. The results represent a meaningful clinical milestone in the competitive GLP-1 obesity drug space. This positions Viking as a credible competitor in one of the fastest-growing drug categories.

tts_summary:
Good morning. This is a company-specific earnings note for Tuesday September 22nd, and there is no broad macro or rates commentary in today's dispatch — it is purely a pre-market earnings and news rundown. Let's get right into it.

Starting with AutoZone. They beat fiscal fourth quarter earnings — $56.05 against the Street's $54.03 — but do not get too excited about the quality here. The beat was largely manufactured by tariff refunds adding 145 basis points to gross margins and a non-cash LIFO benefit adding another 105 basis points. Strip those out and the story looks much weaker. Domestic comps came in at plus 1.6%, well short of the plus 3.1% expected, and operating expenses as a percent of sales worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management did say sales improved in the final eight weeks of the quarter and they feel well positioned for fiscal 2027, but this is a mixed print at best.

Cognex is making a significant acquisition — picking up RealSense, the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for roughly $500 million upfront plus another $106 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80 to $90 million in revenue with more than 50% year-over-year growth. This is a bullish strategic move into high-growth robotics and Physical AI exposure.

MillerKnoll is the cleanest beat in today's batch. They earned 53 cents in fiscal first quarter versus the Street at 36 cents, and importantly, they would have beaten without tariff refund help — stripping out that 11-cent tailwind still leaves 42 cents versus 36 expected. Sales missed, down 3.3% organically, but orders rose 3.5% year-over-year and fiscal 2027 EPS guidance was held unchanged. This is a genuine beat.

THOR Industries missed and the tone from management was cautious. Earnings came in at 78 cents versus 87 expected, gross margins fell 230 basis points to 12.4%, and management pointed to stubborn interest rates, fuel costs, and inflation pressuring retail demand. No formal fiscal 2027 guidance was provided. The silver lining is North American towable RV order backlog surging roughly 75% year-over-year and management talking about durable structural cost cuts — but the headline print is a miss in a tough environment.

Pentair named a new permanent CFO — Bob Hau, effective November 1st. He has prior CFO experience at several large industrials. Routine transition, no guidance update.

Finally, the standout mover this morning is Viking Therapeutics. Shares are spiking in pre-market after positive trial results for their GLP-1 drug VK2735 showed 22% weight loss. That is a headline number that puts Viking squarely in the conversation as a serious competitor in the obesity drug space. Watch this one closely at the open.

Bottom line for today: no broad market directional call in this note, but company-specifically — Viking is the momentum name, MillerKnoll is the quality beat, AutoZone is a headline beat you should fade on quality concerns, and THOR is the cleanest disappointment. Stay focused and trade the tape.
